Anurans of urban ponds in two Brazilian cities

Source: R/data.R
anurans.Rd

Counts of 44 species of anurans in 40 ponds, 20 in Campo Grande (Mato Grosso do Sul) and 20 in São José dos Campos (São Paulo), from the fieldwork of L. B. C. Menezes for chapter 1 of an MSc dissertation (L. B. C. Menezes, M. R. Severgnini & D. B. Provete, unpublished), with the regional pool of each city. The script is data-raw/anurans.R. The counts come from surveys of calling and visual encounter, so their totals depend on effort and detection, and vignette("abc") uses incidence only.

Usage

anurans

Format

List with comm, a matrix of ponds by species with counts; env, a matrix with the hydrology score, area (m²), depth (cm), floating vegetation (%), water temperature (°C) and the urban cover within 1 km in 2022 (%); city, a factor; coords, a matrix with the longitude and latitude of each pond in decimal degrees; pool, a 0/1 matrix of ponds by the 155 species of the regional pools; tree, a phylo object with those species; and grafted, the species added to the tree.

Source

GBIF.org (11 November 2026), occurrence search API; see data-raw/anurans_pool.

Details

The hydrology score is the first principal component of log(x + 1) area, depth, floating vegetation and water temperature, standardised across the 40 ponds and rescaled to 0–100, with larger and deeper ponds at higher scores.

The regional pool of each city has the anurans that breed in lentic water and were recorded both in its ecoregion (Dinerstein et al. 2017: Cerrado for Campo Grande; Alto Paraná Atlantic forests and Serra do Mar coastal forests for São José dos Campos) and within 200 km of its ponds, in occurrences of GBIF (gbif.org, accessed on 11 November 2026, through the occurrence search API; queries in data-raw/anurans_pool), plus the species recorded in its ponds. A species breeds in lentic water if one of its reproductive modes in Nunes-de-Almeida et al. (2021), or in da Silva et al. (2012) for species missing from it, has exotrophic tadpoles in lentic water, or, for species in neither, if at least three congeners are classified and all agree. GBIF records of Leptodactylus latrans were taken as L. luctator, split from it by Magalhães et al. (2020), and the introduced Lithobates catesbeianus was left out.

The tree is the time-calibrated tree of Portik et al. (2023) pruned to the species of the pools, with branch lengths in millions of years and the names of GBIF (so Pithecopus and Ololygon instead of Phyllomedusa and Scinax; Duellman et al. 2016). The tip of L. latrans stands for L. luctator. The six species missing from it (grafted) were joined at the crown of their genus, or of the species of Ololygon in the tree, and the polytomies were resolved at random with branches of length zero.
